```{r set-directories, include=FALSE}
res_dir <- "../results/s06_c_f3_map/"
```

This script combines metadata from the Fortez-Lima et al 2023 paper with our full dataset to create a map showing f3 values for African populations with Mozambique as an African source population and Borneo as an Asian source population.

# Read metadata

```{r echo=FALSE, results='hide', message=FALSE}
dat2 <-
  as.data.frame(
    read_excel("../data/raw/data_input/41586_2023_6770_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx",
      sheet = 2
    )
  )
colnames(dat2) <- dat2[1, ]
dat2 <- dat2[-1, ]
# rename the 'Only-Africa dataset' column
colnames(dat2)[which(colnames(dat2) == "Only-Africa dataset")] <- "Africa"
# include only entries in Africa
dat2 <- dat2 %>%
  filter(Africa == "Yes")
# remove rows with missing lat/lon
dat2 <- dat2 %>%
  filter(!is.na(Latitude) & !is.na(Longitude))
# transform to sf object
dat2 <- st_as_sf(dat2, coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326)
# make sample size numeric
dat2$N <- as.numeric(dat2$N)
```

```{r}
# create plot of Africa
africa <- ne_countries(continent = c("Africa"), scale = 50, returnclass = "sf")
# plot by sample size
p2 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = africa) +
  geom_sf(data = dat2, aes(color = N), size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)) +
  scale_color_viridis_c()
p2
# plot by group
p3 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = africa) +
  geom_sf(data = dat2, aes(color = Group), size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))
p3
# plot by country
p4 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = africa) +
  geom_sf(data = dat2, aes(color = Country), size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))
p4
```

The metadata plotted above contain 111 populations - the data in the 'Only African' dataset in Fortez-Lima et al 2023.

We have some data data from the 'Full-genotyped' dataset as this contains '81 populations with sample sizes lower than 10 individuals'.

Now we read in all sheets in the excel supplementary data to try and get coordinates for all populations in our full dataset.

```{r echo=FALSE, results='hide', message=FALSE}

    )
```

Sheet 9 contains data used in the spatially explicit framework, previously published in: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2859-7 

# Merge metadata

```{r}
# give dat3 and dat4 and dat10 a Country column with value "Unknown"
dat3$Country <- "Unknown"
dat4$Country <- "Unknown"
dat10$Country <- "Unknown"

# remove any duplicates of dat2$population in dat3, dat4, dat9, dat10
dat_2_pops <- dat2$Population
dat3 <- dat3[!dat3$Population %in% dat_2_pops, ]
dat4 <- dat4[!dat4$Population %in% dat_2_pops, ]
dat9 <- dat9[!dat9$Population %in% dat_2_pops, ]
dat10 <- dat10[!dat10$Population %in% dat_2_pops, ]

all_pops <- rbind(dat2, dat3, dat4, dat9, dat10)
dups <- duplicated(all_pops)
# remove duplicates
all_pops <- all_pops[!dups, ]
```

Coordinates are available for 136 populations after merging the metadata.

However, setdiff shows 106 of the populations in NEO_full are not in the metadata!

In some cases the mismatch is a naming issue, eg

 - Namibia_DamaraKSP in dat$`Population label` is probably "Namibia_Damara" in NEO_full)
 - There are coords for Sotho, but in NEO_full there are southern and northern Sotho...
 - SouthAfrica_Coloured in NEO_full is probably SouthAfrica_ColouredAskham in dat$`Population label` - both have 12 individuals

# Add f3's to mad_bor_g1000_sum_ld_no_na

```{r}
# create a subset for each Malagasy population
for (i in unique(adm_f3_african$Malagasy)) {
  malagasy_pop <- i
  subset <- paste0("adm_f3_african_", malagasy_pop)
  assign(subset, adm_f3_african %>% filter(Malagasy == malagasy_pop))
}

# list all the subsets
subset_list <- ls(pattern = "adm_f3_african_")

for (i in subset_list) {
  malagasy_pop <- str_replace(i, "adm_f3_african_", "")
  f3 <- paste0("f3_", malagasy_pop)
  se <- paste0("se_", malagasy_pop)
  dataset <- get(i)
  mad_bor_g1000_sum_ld_no_na <- mad_bor_g1000_sum_ld_no_na %>%
    mutate(!!f3 := dataset$est[match(population, dataset$African)]) %>%
    mutate(!!se := dataset$se[match(population, dataset$African)])
}

mad_bor_g1000_sum_ld_no_na <- mad_bor_g1000_sum_ld_no_na %>%
  filter(!is.na(f3_Betsileo))
```

# Plot f3's on the map: All groups

```{r}
# list all the subsets
subset_list <- ls(pattern = "adm_f3_african_")

plot_maps <- function(subset_list, mad_bor_g1000_sum_ld_no_na, africa) {
  counter <- 1
  plot_list <- list()

  for (i in subset_list) {
    malagasy_pop <- str_replace(i, "adm_f3_african_", "")
    f3 <- paste0("f3_", malagasy_pop)
    se <- paste0("se_", malagasy_pop)

    minimum_f3 <- mad_bor_g1000_sum_ld_no_na %>%
      slice_min(.data[[f3]])
    minval <- unique(as.numeric(minimum_f3[[f3]]))

    upper <- minval + (10 * unique(as.numeric(minimum_f3[[se]])))

    maximum_f3 <- mad_bor_g1000_sum_ld_no_na %>%
      slice_max(.data[[f3]])
    maxval <- unique(as.numeric(maximum_f3[[f3]]))

    this_plot <- ggplot() +
      geom_sf(data = africa) +
      geom_sf(
        data = mad_bor_g1000_sum_ld_no_na,
        aes(
          colour = .data[[f3]],
          shape  = linguistic_group
        ),
        alpha = 0.3, size = 2
      ) +
      scale_color_gradientn(
        colors = rev(viridis::viridis(10)),
        na.value = "grey80",
        limits = c(minval, maxval), # Using the calculated minval
        # Mapping: Purple at min, Yellow at -0.009, End of scale at 0
        values = scales::rescale(c(seq(minval, upper, length.out = 9), maxval)),
        guide = guide_colorbar(barheight = 7),
        oob = scales::squish
      ) +
      coord_sf(crs = st_crs(4326)) +
      theme_minimal() +
      labs(colour = "f3", shape = "Linguistic group") +
      guides(alpha = "none", size = "none") +
      ggtitle(malagasy_pop)

    plot_list[[counter]] <- this_plot
    counter <- counter + 1
  }

  return(plot_list)
}

res_afr <- plot_maps(subset_list, mad_bor_g1000_sum_ld_no_na, africa)

for (p in res_afr) {
  print(p)
  ggsave(paste0(res_dir, "f3_all_african_pops_", p$labels$title, ".jpg"),
    width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300
  )
}

bet_all_afr <- res_afr[[1]]
```

# Plot f3's on the map: Bantu groups

```{r}
plot_bantu_maps <- function(subset_list, mad_bor_g1000_sum_ld_no_na, africa) {
  counter <- 1
  plot_list <- list()

  for (i in subset_list) {
    malagasy_pop <- str_replace(i, "adm_f3_african_", "")
    f3 <- paste0("f3_", malagasy_pop)
    se <- paste0("se_", malagasy_pop)

    mad_bantu <- mad_bor_g1000_sum_ld_no_na %>%
      filter(!bantu_group == "-")

    # minimum f3
    minimum_f3 <- mad_bantu %>%
      slice_min(.data[[f3]])
    minval <- unique(as.numeric(minimum_f3[[f3]]))

    upper <- minval + (10 * unique(as.numeric(minimum_f3[[se]])))

    # maximum f3
    maximum_f3 <- mad_bor_g1000_sum_ld_no_na %>%
      slice_max(.data[[f3]])
    maxval <- unique(as.numeric(maximum_f3[[f3]]))

    this_plot <- ggplot() +
      geom_sf(data = africa) +
      geom_sf(
        data = mad_bantu,
        aes(colour = .data[[f3]], shape = bantu_group),
        alpha = 0.3, size = 2
      ) +
      scale_color_gradientn(
        colors = rev(viridis::viridis(10)),
        na.value = "grey80",
        limits = c(minval, maxval), # Using the calculated minval
        # Mapping: Purple at min, Yellow at -0.009, End of scale at 0
        values = scales::rescale(c(seq(minval, upper, length.out = 9), maxval)),
        guide = guide_colorbar(barheight = 7),
        oob = scales::squish
      ) +
      # make shapes all filled and not hollow
      scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17, 15, 18, 19)) +
      coord_sf(crs = st_crs(4326)) +
      theme_minimal() +
      labs(colour = "f3", shape = "Bantu group") +
      guides(alpha = "none", size = "none") +
      ggtitle(malagasy_pop)

    plot_list[[counter]] <- this_plot
    counter <- counter + 1
  }

  return(plot_list)
}

res_bantu <- plot_bantu_maps(subset_list, mad_bor_g1000_sum_ld_no_na, africa)

for (p in res_bantu) {
  print(p)
  ggsave(paste0(res_dir, "f3_bantu_pops_", p$labels$title, ".jpg"),
    width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300
  )
}

bet_bantu_afr <- res_bantu[[1]]
```
